facts.raw_span: A 68-year-old man
pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
no pain with ocular movements
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography of the right eye revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma

pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
no pain with ocular movements
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography of the right eye revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma

concepts.why: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the findings on anterior segment optical coherence tomography are consistent with fungal keratitis.
The history of DSAEK and the presence of keratitis with no conjunctival hyperemia or discharge suggest an immune-mediated process.
The patient's history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa and the presence of brown, multilobular lesions in the cornea are consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's history of DSAEK and the development of keratitis with a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers are consistent with this diagnosis.

rationales.F03: Recent DSAEK surgery increases the risk of post-DSAEK keratitis.
rationales.F04: History of Thaumetopoea pityocampa eye infection increases the risk of Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis.
rationales.F08: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma are characteristic of fungal keratitis and Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis.
rationales.F12: Central and peripheral infiltrates in the cornea are consistent with keratitis, particularly fungal keratitis and post-DSAEK keratitis.
